scope: N+1 risks on KDS list + items-board, index coverage on (branch_id, status, order_datetime) hot KDS query
method: read-only analysis of Eloquent queries + migrations + cast contracts

findings.title: Items-board orderItems() eager-loads ALL relations on all orders but does NOT pre-load orderItem (the Item model) — N+1 risk on every chef pluck
findings.consequence: For 50 active orders × N items each (avg 3), that is potentially 150 Item::find() queries on every items-board poll. The today-orders path (KDSOrderDetailsResource :46) DOES loadMissing('orderItem') inside the resource collection. The items-board path does NOT — the OrderItem rows are pluck'd via $orders->pluck('orderItems')->flatten() then groupBy'd, with no Item::eager-load. Hot KDS poll = N+1.
findings.fix_proposal: Add ->with(['orderItems.orderItem']) on the orderItems() query OR loadMissing inside KDSOrderItemsResource similar to KDSOrderDetailsResource:46. The latter is cleaner because it mirrors the today-orders path.
findings.estimated_impact: Per-poll: ~150 extra queries × poll-frequency ~5s = ~30 qps superfluous, single branch.
findings.owner_call_v1_0_x: Quick win; sentinel test = $this->assertSameNumber(N expected) using DB::enableQueryLog()

findings.title: Index coverage on hot KDS query is correct — idx_orders_branch_status + idx_orders_datetime cover the active window

evidence.hot_query_shape: WHERE status IN (...) AND branch_id = ? AND order_datetime BETWEEN ? AND ?

findings.consequence: MySQL planner can pick idx_orders_branch_status for the (status, branch_id) leading prefix, then range-scan order_datetime. Wave 3b commit 148dbebce specifically swapped whereDate (non-sargable) → whereBetween (sargable). Indexes covered.

findings.title: Missing composite (branch_id, status, order_datetime) — covering index would short-circuit the active window query but is V1.0.X optimization

evidence.ideal: (branch_id, status, order_datetime) covering all three filter columns

findings.consequence: Today MySQL picks idx_orders_branch_status, intersects with idx_orders_datetime via index_merge if available. Acceptable at V1 scale (1 restaurant). At V2 (multi-tenant SaaS) this becomes a tier-3 optimization candidate.

findings.title: groupBy in items-board service runs in PHP (Collection), not in DB — DB returns N rows, PHP allocates a temp hash table of all order_items per poll
findings.consequence: Memory pressure: O(items × order_items.json_payload_size). At 50 orders × 3 items = 150 rows = trivial. At 500 orders (worst-case advance backlog) × 5 items = 2500 rows = still cheap. Not a leak, but architecturally fragile if the active-window grows (the limit(51) + advance carry-over could yield more). The TZ heal commit 148dbebce keeps the window bounded daily, so OK at V1.

findings.title: Cast contract verified — composition_snapshot + allergens_snapshot both cast to 'array'
findings.consequence: Resource code can safely access $this->allergens_snapshot expecting array. The safeJsonDecodeArray helper in KDSOrderItemsResource:55 is defensive belt-and-suspenders (handles already-array AND string-JSON cases). Good defensive style.

verdict.summary: Indexes cover the hot path. One latent N+1 on items-board (PK-3-DBA-01) is the most impactful finding. Memory + scan are bounded at V1 scale. No DB-level blocker for V1.
